title: My, your, our: -ni, -si, -mme, -nne
focus: A possessive ending is a short ending on the noun that tells us its owner. For these regular singular nouns, attach -ni, -si, -mme, or -nne to the complete basic noun.

exercises.prompt: Choose the noun in “my ball”: minun ___. Use pallo (“ball”).
exercises.explanation: pallo + -ni = palloni. Choose the ending matching minun.
exercises.misconceptionCategory: First- and second-person possessive endings: form or meaning confused

optionFeedback.palloni: pallo + -ni = palloni. Choose the ending matching minun.
optionFeedback.pallo: A personal owner phrase needs a matching noun ending in standard written Finnish.
optionFeedback.pallosi: This ending does not match the requested owner or the noun’s vowel harmony.

answerDiagnostics.category: First- and second-person possessive endings: predictable form error
answerDiagnostics.explanation: Keep the basic noun and add its possessive ending. The owner pronoun does not replace that ending.
